brief: The vendor/supplier indirect route is unusually productive for Slovenia because the market's technology supply is concentrated and the suppliers advertise loudly. Two anchors dominate: HRC d.o.o. (Hibis), a domestic core-banking vendor that publicly names essentially the whole second tier of SI banks and savings banks and claims >50% market share, and Bankart, the shared processor whose supplier choices (Diebold Nixdorf Vynamic replacing Base24; Nets/Nexi RealTime24/7 behind instant payments) are disclosed in vendor and IR press releases with estate scope and country counts. Around them sit ATM/self-service and terminal players (Printec/NCR, Diebold Nixdorf, Euronet as independent deployer, Payten/ASEE), Temenos at NLB, and Halcom whose e-banking pages publish rare volume proxies and a bank-coverage roster. Main weaknesses of this cell in this pass: no card-personalisation or cash-logistics vendor route was established, no Slovenia-specific Nexi/Worldline acquiring announcement was found, kontron-slovenia.com was unreadable due to a TLS chain error (unverified, not dead), and the session's search budget ran out before Payten-SI and Flik-supplier queries could run.
